commit_message:
Workers record every failure and always run the middleware release hook (#13)

* Workers record every failure and always run the middleware release hook (#12)

ThreadBackend, ProcessBackend's worker and the queue entrypoint each carried
their own copy of compute/record/hooks, and all three caught only Exception
and wrote RUNNING outside the try. One _compute_and_record now runs in all
three: a BaseException is recorded FAILED then re-raised, a failing store
write (RUNNING, COMPLETED or FAILED) still ends in on_error, and exactly one
of after_compute / on_error follows every before_compute. The three hook
loops become one _call_hooks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review fixes: a cancellation is final, hooks cannot strand each other (#12)

- The worker's COMPLETED/FAILED write no longer overwrites a CANCELLED record
  (a cancelled job ending in a BaseException used to leave CANCELLED; the
  first pass turned it into FAILED).
- _call_hooks runs every middleware even when one raises a BaseException,
  then re-raises it; before_compute runs inside the try, so a hook interrupt
  is recorded FAILED and still followed by on_error.
- FileSystemStore keeps the exception type name when str(error) is empty.
- Hook and record failures are logged with tracebacks.
- Tests: cancellation is final, interrupting hooks, the queue path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-review fixes: a failed read never loses a finished job (#12)

- _record_unless_cancelled treats a failing read as "not cancelled" and
  returns what the store holds, so after_compute sees CANCELLED, not the
  refused COMPLETED.
- _call_hooks keeps the first BaseException without relying on truthiness
  and logs any later one.
- cancel()'s docstring states the new rule and its remaining race.
- The cancellation test asserts the raise and which hook ran.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
